In this section, we try to create a regression table using some helpful functions from [`gtsummary`](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/){target="_blank"}

We start by choosing the relevant columns to make the regression table, keeping rows with a birth outcome (Non-live birth and Live birth).

```{webr}
#| label: load opt data
#| envir: table_3
#| autorun: true
opt_data <- readRDS("data/opt_data.rds") |> 
  dplyr::filter(
    .data[["Birth.outcome"]] %in% c("Non-live birth", "Live birth")
  )
```

## Birth Weight Regression Table

### Data Required

Here is the dataset required. To recall, we set 

- `Birthweight_2500_regression` be
   - `NA` if `Birthweight` is `NA`.
   - `1` if `Birthweight` is less than 2500.
   - `0` otherwise.

```{webr}
#| label: data for birth weight regression table
#| envir: table_3
#| autorun: true
opt_birth_weight_for_regression_data <- opt_data |> 
  dplyr::select(
    c("PID", "Group", "Age",
      "Education", "Hypertension", "Diabetes",
      "Birthweight", "Birthweight_2500_regression")
  )

opt_birth_weight_for_regression_data |> 
  reactable::reactable(
    filterable = TRUE,
    paginationType = "jump",
    defaultPageSize = 5,
    minRows = 5)
```

### Create Regression Results

We create a univariable logistic regression model using just the `Group` column and the outcome `Birthweight_2500_regression`.

```{webr}
#| caption: birthweight unadjusted model
#| label: birthweight unadjusted model
#| envir: table_3
#| autorun: true
birthweight_unadjusted_model <- glm(
  Birthweight_2500_regression ~ Group,
  data   = opt_data,
  family = binomial
)

broom::tidy(birthweight_unadjusted_model)
```

We can display the regression results using the [`tbl_regression`](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/tbl_regression.html){target="_blank"}. Setting `exponentiate = TRUE` will convert the predictors' raw coefficient into odds ratio.

In addition, we can display the number of patients that enters the model using [`add_n`](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/add_n_summary.html){target="_blank"}.

[`add_nevent`](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/add_nevent_regression.html){target="_blank"} provides the number of events (Number of patients with `Birthweight_2500_regression` equal to `1` or have a live birth weight of less than 2500g).

```{webr}
#| caption: birthweight unadjusted model result table
#| label: birthweight unadjusted model result table
#| envir: table_3
#| autorun: true
birthweight_unadjusted_table <- birthweight_unadjusted_model |> 
  gtsummary::tbl_regression(
    exponentiate = TRUE
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::add_n(
    location = c("level")
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::add_nevent(
    location = c("level")
  )

birthweight_unadjusted_table
```

We create a multivariable logistic regression model using additional columns (`Group`, `Age`, `Education`, `Hypertension`, `Diabetes`) and the outcome `Birthweight_2500_regression`.

```{webr}
#| caption: birthweight adjusted model
#| label: birthweight adjusted model
#| envir: table_3
#| autorun: true
birthweight_adjusted_model <- glm(
  Birthweight_2500_regression ~ Group + Age + Education + Hypertension + Diabetes,
  data   = opt_data,
  family = binomial
)

```

We display the regression results using the same three functions.

```{webr}
#| caption: birthweight adjusted model result table
#| label: birthweight adjusted model result table
#| envir: table_3
#| autorun: true
birthweight_adjusted_table <- birthweight_adjusted_model |> 
  gtsummary::tbl_regression(
    exponentiate = TRUE
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::add_n(
    location = c("level")
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::add_nevent(
    location = c("level")
  )

birthweight_adjusted_table
```

## Pregnancy Duration Regression Table

### Data Required

Here is the dataset required. To recall, we set 

- `Preg_duration_37_regression` be
   - `1` if `GA.at.outcome.weeks` is less than 37.
   - `0` otherwise.
   
### Create Regression Results

We create a univariable logistic regression model using just the `Group` column and the outcome `Preg_duration_37_regression`.

```{webr}
#| caption: pregnancy duration unadjusted model
#| label: pregnancy duration unadjusted model
#| envir: table_3
#| autorun: true
preg_duration_unadjusted_model <- glm(
  Preg_duration_37_regression ~ Group,
  data   = opt_data,
  family = binomial
)

preg_duration_unadjusted_table <- preg_duration_unadjusted_model |> 
  gtsummary::tbl_regression(
    exponentiate = TRUE
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::add_n(
    location = c("level")
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::add_nevent(
    location = c("level")
  )
```

We create a multivariable logistic regression model using additional columns (`Group`, `Age`, `Education`, `Hypertension`, `Diabetes`) and the outcome `Preg_duration_37_regression`.

```{webr}
#| caption: pregnancy duration adjusted model
#| label: pregnancy duration adjusted model
#| envir: table_3
#| autorun: true
preg_duration_adjusted_model <- glm(
  Preg_duration_37_regression ~ Group + Age + Education + Hypertension + Diabetes,
  data   = opt_data,
  family = binomial
)

preg_duration_adjusted_table <- preg_duration_adjusted_model |> 
  gtsummary::tbl_regression(
    exponentiate = TRUE
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::add_n(
    location = c("level")
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::add_nevent(
    location = c("level")
  )

preg_duration_adjusted_table
```

## Combine

We can combine the birth weight and pregnancy duration regression table by column using the [`tbl_merge`](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/tbl_merge.html){target="_blank"}

```{webr}
#| caption: combine unadjusted regression results table
#| label: combine unadjusted regression results table
#| envir: table_3
#| autorun: true
unadjusted_table <- gtsummary::tbl_merge(
  tbls = list(birthweight_unadjusted_table, preg_duration_unadjusted_table),
  tab_spanner = c("**Birth Weight <2500 g**", "**Pregnant Duration <37 wk**")
)

unadjusted_table
```

```{webr}
#| caption: combine adjusted regression results table
#| label: combine adjusted regression results table
#| envir: table_3
#| autorun: true
adjusted_table <- gtsummary::tbl_merge(
  tbls = list(birthweight_adjusted_table, preg_duration_adjusted_table),
  tab_spanner = c("**Birth Weight <2500 g**", "**Pregnant Duration <37 wk**")
)

adjusted_table
```

Finally, we can combine the univariable and multivariable regression results table using the [gtsummary::tbl_stack](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/tbl_stack.html){target="_blank"}

```{webr}
#| caption: combine regression results table
#| label: combine regression results table
#| envir: table_3
#| autorun: true
combined_table <- gtsummary::tbl_stack(
  list(unadjusted_table, adjusted_table),
  group_header = c("Unadjusted", "Adjusted by Age, Education, Hypertension and Diabetes")
)

combined_table
```
